memory_update.text: LOPE and ATGE are the primary reference companies for direct public exposure to healthcare licensure education and hybrid clinical-program capacity.
CAE is a second-order underfollowed supplier candidate because healthcare simulation labs may become a practical capacity-release valve when clinical placements and faculty are scarce.

PSO/Pearson VUE is a regulated testing-infrastructure candidate tied to NCLEX and healthcare certification workflows; validate healthcare licensure contribution within Pearson VUE revenue before upgrading.

Many highly relevant clinical-placement software, nursing test-prep, simulation and healthcare-education workflow vendors appear private, including CORE Higher Ed, myClinicalExchange, InPlace, Laerdal, Gaumard and several clinical-placement networks; public-market mapping may therefore require indirect owners or acquirers.

HSTM should be carried forward as the highest-priority underfollowed candidate for the healthcare-licensure / hybrid-campus capacity node because it directly overlaps clinical education, credentialing, simulation-based education, and clinical-rotation management.

CAE should be carried forward as a simulation-equipment / healthcare-training supplier, but later layers must test segment materiality because healthcare simulation may be small relative to aviation and defense.
PSO should be carried forward as a regulated testing-infrastructure candidate through Pearson VUE / NCLEX, with materiality and contract economics as the primary evidence gaps.

LOPE is useful as a reference demand and capacity anchor, not as the main underfollowed supplier; its disclosures support the thesis that hybrid healthcare education may be constrained by licensure, clinical placements, simulation labs, and campus utilization.

Several important clinical-placement and healthcare-education suppliers appear private or not clearly US-listed, including InPlace Software, CAUHEC Connect, CORE Higher Ed, Precepta, UWorld, Laerdal, and Ascend Learning; later passes should track whether any public parent, IPO path, or listed distributor exists.

Keep LOPE as the reference anchor for healthcare licensure and hybrid campus capacity because supplied evidence directly ties its ABSN/OTA programs to simulation technology, VR, prerequisites, employer partnerships, and licensure pathways.

Add ATGE as a direct healthcare workforce education candidate; its Chamberlain and Walden assets may provide a cleaner nursing/social-work/healthcare licensure exposure than generic online education screens suggest.

Add UTI as an underfollowed healthcare education capacity candidate through Concorde Career Colleges; ticker-level screens may miss the allied-health, dental, nursing, patient-care, and diagnostic training exposure.

Add LRN as a second-order credentialing/certification candidate through MedCerts; relevance is weaker than ABSN/OTA operators and must be tested against accreditation, state eligibility, externship requirements, and recognized certification outcomes.

Pure-play healthcare simulation vendors such as Laerdal and Gaumard appear private; CAE Healthcare was found as a simulation reference but needs separate verification for current ownership/materiality before adding CAE as a public-equity candidate.

Next Layer 1C/2 work should verify clinical placement software, simulation lab suppliers, NCLEX/TEAS/HESI test-prep suppliers, accreditation vendors, and state-board approval dependencies, because this pass found stronger public operators than pure public suppliers.

LOPE should remain the reference anchor for healthcare licensure and hybrid-campus capacity because its disclosures directly mention ABSN/OTA graduates, hybrid growth, simulation technology, virtual reality, employer agreements, and state-specific licensure requirements.

CAE is a high-quality underfollowed supplier candidate for this node because healthcare simulation is buried inside a broader aviation/defense simulation company, yet its products map directly to nursing and medical-school simulation labs.

ATGE is a healthcare-education capacity candidate rather than a generic online-learning name; later layers should test clinical placement, accreditation, licensing outcomes, and program-level enrollment growth.

NNI is a speculative shadow candidate: campus commerce, higher-ed payments, and Vosaic observation tools could support hybrid healthcare education infrastructure, but the healthcare-program linkage needs named-customer or use-case evidence.

Many pure-play clinical placement, nursing simulation, healthcare VR, and licensure-prep vendors appear to be private, so public-market mapping may require parent-company, supplier, or infrastructure proxies rather than obvious tickers.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the healthcare licensure and hybrid-campus-capacity node. The cleanest reference exposures are education-service operators that own or service nursing/allied-health program capacity, while the underfollowed lane points to simulation-lab equipment/software and licensure-testing infrastructure. The current pass intentionally avoids broad mega-cap online-learning names unless their exposure is directly tied to clinical capacity, simulation, healthcare credentialing, or regulated licensure workflows. Expanded the healthcare-licensure / hybrid-campus capacity node toward scarce suppliers and regulated infrastructure rather than generic online education. The strongest underfollowed public-market exposure found in this pass is HealthStream, because it touches clinical education, credentialing, simulation-based education, and clinical-rotation management. CAE is a simulation-equipment and healthcare-training infrastructure supplier, but healthcare is likely a smaller segment inside a larger aviation/defense simulation business. Pearson is a regulated testing infrastructure anchor through Pearson VUE / NCLEX, with less pure exposure but high chokepoint relevance. Grand Canyon Education is included only as a reference capacity operator because its disclosures directly mention ABSN/OTA hybrid growth, simulation technology, virtual reality, state licensure needs, and employer pipelines. Expanded the US-listed universe around healthcare licensure and hybrid campus capacity. The strongest public-market mapping is not pure online content del
